# load packages
library(tidyverse)

There are 77 files for each dataframe, so I needed to figure out a way to make a vector for them. That way read_csv could read all 77 and put them together already: https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/base/versions/3.6.2/topics/list.files. 

```{r}
list.files("../raw_data")

details_files <- list.files("../raw_data", pattern = "^details.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
length(details_files)

fatal_files <- list.files("../raw_data", pattern = "^fatal.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
length(details_files)

details_data <- read_csv(details_files)

fatal_data <- read_csv(fatal_files)

storm_fatal_data <- left_join(fatal_data, details_data, join_by(EVENT_ID))
```


```{r}
#shortening dataset columns
storm_fatal_format <- storm_fatal_data |>
  select(!c(FAT_YEARMONTH, FAT_DAY, FAT_TIME, BEGIN_YEARMONTH, BEGIN_DAY, BEGIN_TIME, END_YEARMONTH, END_DAY, END_TIME, SOURCE, CZ_TYPE, WFO, CATEGORY, BEGIN_DATE_TIME, END_DATE_TIME)) 

#use this code for making graphs and other non spatial visualizations
write_csv(storm_fatal_format, "../data/storm_fatal_combined.csv")
```

```{r}
#code for mapping fatalities
data_geo_start <- storm_fatal_format |>
  drop_na(BEGIN_LON, BEGIN_LAT) |>
  mutate(fatality_date = as.Date(FATALITY_DATE, format = "%m/%d/%Y"), 
    deaths = n(),
    deaths_direct = sum(FATALITY_TYPE == "D"), 
    deaths_indirect = sum(FATALITY_TYPE == "I"),
    deaths_female = sum(FATALITY_SEX == "F", na.rm = TRUE),
    deaths_male = sum(FATALITY_SEX == "M", na.rm = TRUE),
    median_age = median(FATALITY_AGE, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .by = EVENT_ID) |>
  distinct(EVENT_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) |> select(-starts_with("fatality_")) |>
  mutate(ID = str_to_lower(STATE),
         country_zone = str_to_title(CZ_NAME), contiguous_us = between(BEGIN_LON, -125, -66) & between(BEGIN_LAT, 24, 50)) 

#use this dataset for making maps
write_csv(data_geo_start, "../data/FINAL_wrangled_storm.csv")
```



```{r}
#wrangling for graphs displaying property and crop damages

#converting K and M to numbers, used resource: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61987917/how-do-i-replace-k-and-m-with-thousands-and-millions
damages_numeric <- storm_fatal_format |>
 separate(DAMAGE_PROPERTY,into = c("value","modifier"),
           sep = "(?<=[\\d])(?=[^\\d.])") |>
  mutate(modifier = case_when(
                              modifier == "M" ~ 1000000,
                              modifier == "K" ~ 1000,
                              TRUE ~ 1),
         result_property= as.numeric(value) * modifier) |>
  separate(DAMAGE_CROPS,into = c("value","modifier"),
           sep = "(?<=[\\d])(?=[^\\d.])") |>
  mutate(modifier = case_when(
                              modifier == "M" ~ 1000000,
                              modifier == "K" ~ 1000,
                              TRUE ~ 1),
         result_crops= as.numeric(value) * modifier)


#dataset for graph
damages <- damages_numeric |>
  group_by(EVENT_TYPE, STATE, YEAR) |>
  summarize(
    total_property = sum(result_property),
    total_crops = sum(result_crops),
    per_month_property = total_property/12,
    per_month_crops = total_crops/12
  )

#saving data
write_csv(damages, "../data/damages.csv")
```


```{r}
#wrangling for graphing storm type per year per state

storm_type_state <- storm_fatal_format |>
  group_by(EVENT_TYPE, STATE, YEAR) |>
  summarize(
    N = n()
  )

#wrangling for graphing storm type per year
storm_type_per_year <- storm_fatal_format |>
  group_by(EVENT_TYPE, YEAR) |>
  summarize(
    N = n()
  )

#saving data
write_csv(storm_type_state, "../data/storm_type_state.csv")
write_csv(storm_type_per_year, "../data/storm_type_year.csv")
```

```{r}
#wrangling for tornado specific information

#summarizing average length and width of tornados by state and year
tornado_state <- storm_fatal_format |>
  filter(EVENT_TYPE == "Tornado") |>
  group_by(STATE, YEAR) |>
  summarize(
    length = mean(TOR_LENGTH), 
    width = mean(TOR_WIDTH),
  )

#summarizing average length and width of tornados by year
tornado_year <- storm_fatal_format |>
  filter(EVENT_TYPE == "Tornado") |>
  group_by(YEAR) |>
  summarize(
    length = mean(TOR_LENGTH),
    width = mean(TOR_WIDTH)
  )

#saving data
write_csv(tornado_state, "../data/tornado_state.csv")
write_csv(tornado_year, "../data/tornado_year.csv")
```

```{r}
#dataset with count of each type of storm each year (using in bar charts)

stormcount <- data_geo_start |>
  select(YEAR, EVENT_TYPE) |>
  #making each combo of year/event into one string
  unite(storm, YEAR, EVENT_TYPE, sep = ",") |>
  #counting those to get the total amount of each
  count(storm) |>
  #splitting back into 2 columns
  separate(storm, into = c("YEAR", "EVENT_TYPE"), sep = ",")

write_csv(stormcount, "../data/stormcount.csv")
```
